# Summary


**Introduction**:
Volatile anaesthetics contribute to the environmental footprint of operating rooms.
CONTRAfluran^TM^ (ZeoSys Medical GmbH, Luckenwalde, Germany)
passively captures sevoflurane at the anaesthesia machine exhaust port
for thermal desorption and pharmaceutical reuse.
The relative amount of sevoflurane that can be recaptured remains unclear.
The only study reporting a capture efficiency found
markedly different values in its two operating rooms.
We therefore conducted the first multicentre study to identify the
real-world capture efficiency of the CONTRAfluran system.

**Methods**:
In this prospective, multicentre observational study, we analysed the capture
efficiency for
`r n_agcs["final"]` of `r n_agcs["initial"]` CONTRAfluran canisters.
These were used in
`r n_ors["final"]` operating rooms across `r n_center["final"]` hospitals
in Germany and Austria
from `r format(lubridate::floor_date(study_period[1L], "month"), "%B %Y")`
to `r format(lubridate::floor_date(study_period[2L], "month"), "%B %Y")`.

**Results**:
The `r n_agcs["final"]` canisters
were in place during `r n_cases["final"]` anaesthesia cases
of which `r n_cases_inhalational` used inhalational anaesthesia.
ZeoSys recovered `r round(zeosys_sevo_weight_kg, 1)` kg of sevoflurane.
This corresponds to an estimated capture efficiency of `r round(recovery_pct_final, 1)`%.

**Discussion**:
CONTRAfluran canisters recaptured approximately
`r round(recovery_pct_final, 0)`%
of administered sevoflurane under routine clinical conditions.
This is lower than the 34% of our previous single-centre study
but within the range observed between its two operating rooms.

**Keywords**:
inhalational anaesthesia; sevoflurane; vapour capture technology; capture efficiency
